subject: what to specify as prior with inverse_wishart, cov_prior * scale or cov_prior in STAN?

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: what to specify as prior with inverse_wishart, cov_prior * scale or cov_prior in STAN?
parts:
Dear all,

I made a test with the inverse_wishart. If I know a prior-covariance matrix in cov_prior,
do I specify cov_prior*scale or cov_prior?

In
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/0gqVgxv5B40/9RtYwLXljikJ
E[inv_wishart(nu,S)] = S / (nu - k - 1)

cov_prior*scale is not stable in a more complex model, whereas cov_prior is.
I'm confused.

Please help.
Andre

library(rstan)
scode <- "
data {
  int<lower = 0> V;
  real DF;
  matrix[V,V] cov_prior;
}
parameters {
  cov_matrix[V] Omega;
}
model {
  Omega ~ inv_wishart(DF, cov_prior);
 
}
"
V <- 7
DF <- 9
scale <-  (DF - V - 1)
cov_prior <- diag(V)
foo_data <- list(            V = V,
                 DF = DF,
                 cov_prior = cov_prior*scale )
 
 
foo <- stan(model_code = scode, data = foo_data, chains = 1, iter = 10000, control=list(adapt_delta=0.98))
apply(extract(foo,"Omega")$Omega,c(2,3),mean)

messages.subject: Re: what to specify as prior with inverse_wishart, cov_prior * scale or cov_prior in STAN?
parts:
On Wednesday, October 19, 2016 at 2:13:18 AM UTC-4, andre.p...@googlemail.com wrote:
I made a test with the inverse_wishart. If I know a prior-covariance matrix in cov_prior,
do I specify cov_prior*scale or cov_prior?

The second argument to inv_wishart should be S rather than S / (nu - k - 1). But the poor performance is one of the reasons we don't recommend using inv_wishart. If you were going to use it, I would probably use the transformed parameters block to take the inverse of a matrix that has a Wishart prior.

Ben

I ended up with the Barlett decomposition of the wishart distribution.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wishart_distribution#Bartlett_decomposition

it allow me to control factors of the wishart distribution. Since the matrix is
triangular. The inverse is easy by backward substitution. 

Andre

parameterization of Wishart and inverse Wishart, which we in turn
need if they're ever going to be robust or efficient. There's
all sorts of fun coding and Jacobian calculations for whoever
wants to take this one on :-)

- Bob
